TOGAF® 系列指南说明如何使用TOGAF标准，以及如何调整它以满足具体需要。

系列指南预期是TOGAF标准中发展最快的部分，定位为标准的指导部分。TOGAF基础内容预期保持长期稳定，而使用指导可以针对行业、架构风格、用途和问题。例如，支持扩展企业转型所需的利益相关者、关注点、视图和支撑模型，可能与将内部IT环境迁移到云所需的内容显著不同；两者都使用ADM，都从架构愿景开始，开发目标架构，并走向实施与迁移计划。TOGAF基础内容仍是跨行业、领域和风格的必要支架。

source_units.text_en: About the TOGAF® Series Guides
The TOGAF® Series Guides contain guidance on how to use the TOGAF Standard and how to adapt it to fulfill specific needs.

The TOGAF® Series Guides are expected to be the most rapidly developing part of the TOGAF Standard and are positioned as the guidance part of the standard. While the TOGAF Fundamental Content is expected to be long-lived and stable, guidance on the use of the TOGAF Standard can be industry, architectural style, purpose, and problem-specific. For example, the stakeholders, concerns, views, and supporting models required to support the transformation of an extended enterprise may be significantly different than those used to support the transition of an in-house IT environment to the cloud; both will use the Architecture Development Method (ADM), start with an Architecture Vision, and develop a Target Architecture on the way to an Implementation and Migration Plan. The TOGAF Fundamental Content remains the essential scaffolding across industry, domain, and style.

source_units.text_en: 1. Introduction
In this document, information architecture best practices are shared to support architecture work on the specific topic of Metadata Management. It aims to provide a framework to:
• Accelerate the delivery of architecture study
• Inform Data Architects and other data professionals about good practices
• Provide a common language to describe the Metadata Management capability to data professionals: Chief Data Officers, Data Managers, Architects, Data Engineers, and Data Scientists

Metadata Management is instrumental in delivering value from data. This document intends also to emphasize the benefits of data documentation, and the necessary efforts required to set up an effective Metadata Management capability within an organization.

本文档使用 ArchiMate 规范 [C226] 的正式记法描述元数据管理架构参考模型。所用元素见图 2-1，定义如下：

**动机方面**

- **目标**（Goal）：对组织及其利益相关者而言，关于意图、方向或期望终态的高层陈述。
- **需求**（Requirement）：定义适用于架构所描述特定系统之属性的需求陈述。

**业务层**

- **业务角色**（Business Role）：代表执行特定行为的责任，可把参与者分配给该角色，或代表参与者在特定行动/事件中所扮演的部分。
- **业务功能**（Business Function）：基于一组选定标准（通常是所需业务资源和/或胜任力）的业务行为集合，与组织紧密对齐，但不一定由组织显式治理。
- **业务协作**（Business Collaboration）：两个或以上业务内部主动结构要素的聚合，共同执行集体行为。

**应用层**

- **应用功能**（Application Function）：可由应用组件执行的自动化行为。

source_units.text_en: 2.1. The ArchiMate® Specification
This document uses the formal notation from the ArchiMate Specification [C226] to describe the Metadata Management architecture reference models.
The ArchiMate elements used in this document are shown in Figure 2-1.
Figure 2-1: The ArchiMate Modeling Notation Elements Used in This Document
The ArchiMate definitions of each concept used in this document are as follows:
Motivation Aspect
• Goal: represents a high-level statement of intent, direction, or desired end state for an organization and its stakeholders
• Requirement: represents a statement of need defining a property that applies to a specific system as described by the architecture
Business Layer
• Business role: represents the responsibility for performing specific behavior, to which an actor can be assigned, or the part an actor plays in a particular action or event

• Business function: represents a collection of business behavior based on a chosen set of criteria (typically required business resources and/or competencies), closely aligned to an organization, but not necessarily explicitly governed by the organization
• Business Collaboration: represents an aggregate of two or more business internal active structure elements that work together to perform collective behavior
Application Layer
• Application function: represents automated behavior that can be performed by an application
component

sections.translation_zh:
简单地说，元数据可以称为“关于数据的数据”。例如，元数据表明数据的作者/创建者、创建时间、安全分级、数据质量属性等。根据《数据管理知识体系》（DMBOK2）第 417 页：

> “元数据帮助组织理解其数据、系统与工作流。它使质量评估成为可能，是数据库及其他应用管理不可或缺的部分；它有助于处理、维护、集成、保护、审计与治理其他数据的能力。”

元数据概念并不新鲜，IT 业界广泛用它定义“关于数据的数据”。早在数字时代之前的古代，作者、标题、泥板数量等元数据就已用于编目泥板藏品。因此，元数据提供额外信息，以便更好地了解和使用数据。

**元数据管理**是使高质量、集成元数据可被访问的规划、实施与控制活动 [DMBOK2]。它用额外信息增强数据，使其可用于：

- **了解你的数据**：
  - 减少数据的不确定性与可能的误解；
  - 了解可用数据的质量及相关业务规则（数据质量业务规则、转换业务规则等）；
  - 了解数据来源与使用情况；
  - 改进 BI 报表审计；
  - 监控整个信息系统的数据量，以降低环境影响。
- **管理数据风险并符合监管要求**：
  - 利用数据分级（保密性、隐私）支持数据风险管理（如支持数据保护影响评估），基于已定义元数据建立数据访问模型（角色、用户责任、处理目的等）；
  - 为企业最有价值的资产利用安全与隐私元数据，例如：安全元数据支持从以网络为中心转向以属性为中心的安全（如零信任等新标准把数据视为企业资产）；企业身份管理依赖联邦身份（共同属性）控制人或机器对数据的访问；许多国家/地区的隐私立法（如欧盟）使可识别个人数据的传播成为非法；
  - 改进数据血缘与使用审计，以满足监管要求。
- **管理数据生命周期**：
  - 需要元数据表明遵循企业政策与指令所需的内容；
  - 需要知道哪些必须归档并作为记录保留（往往是国家立法的要求）；
  - 需要识别保留生命周期以触发处置（删除）。
- **缩短上市时间**：
  - 对任何新业务举措，借助良好的数据文档（术语表、字典、分级）减少数据范围界定工作；
  - 识别用例所需的相关数据元素。
- **管理数据质量与共享**：
  - 实现信息互操作/共享，促进企业及扩展企业的协作、共享（态势感知）与决策支持；
  - 识别冗余与过时数据；
  - 支持业务利用外部数据。

元数据常被推给 IT，但它本质上是业务关注点。2000 年代中期大量调查及新的政府立法之后，元数据已成为必须维护的关键企业资产，以确保股东透明度、企业安全与客户隐私。

NoSQL 数据库（宽松数据模式）的兴起与近期大数据趋势承诺从任何数据中释放价值，导致人们只关注建设采集、存储与分析数据的能力，很少投入元数据——常被视为无关紧要，或认为机器学习工具可自动获得。除市场趋势外，元数据管理在许多组织中仍是挑战，原因包括：

- **IT 复杂性**：遗留应用文档匮乏（参考数据缺失，数据在应用生命周期内含义变化）；并购扩大 IT 架构，需文档化的元数据范围随之变化；复制因子（某数据元素在信息系统中被复制的次数）越高，元数据文档化越难。
- **数据复杂性**：采集数据的多样性与速度（近实时社交媒体或日志、用于机器学习的文本与图像等）需要新技术采集相关元数据；动态模式使保持元数据文档最新变得困难。
- **IT 营销趋势**：微服务/微应用常挑战数据血缘并提高复制因子；“敏捷”交付被错误理解为不需要文档。
- **人工工作**：如何与业务及IT中小企业（原文为Small and Medium Enterprises，SMEs）一起采集信息？正确的粒度与优先级标准是什么？元数据校验不自动，需要人工复核。
- **缺乏数据标准**：命名约定；数据类型与单位约定。

然而从业务视角看，元数据是良好了解和理解组织已有数据的关键。因此，对任何希望高效利用数据的组织而言，元数据是重要的基础数据管理能力。

在设计该能力时，我们聚焦有效交付元数据管理所需的最小功能集。随着组织实践成熟，可超越本框架定义的基线。我们还认为，数据的伦理使用对每个组织都越来越重要——这体现在 GDPR（《通用数据保护条例》，2018 年 5 月 25 日在欧盟生效）之后世界多地出台的法规中。比合规更重要的是，按设计记录数据使用、以实现对数据伦理使用的治理，可成为组织的竞争优势。因此，本基线框架在元数据管理业务功能中纳入了“数据使用文档”，并强调个人数据。

本节介绍高层参考模型功能及其定义。更详细的功能见本文档第 5 章与 5.2 节的参考模型部分。

source_units.text_en: 3. Metadata Management Capability

Simplistically, metadata can be called “data about data”. For example, metadata indicates who is the author/creator of the data, when it was created, its security classification, its data quality attributes, and so on. According to the Data Management Body of Knowledge (DMBOK2), pp.417 [DMBOK2]:

“Metadata helps an organization understand its data, its systems, and its workflows. It enables quality assessment and is integral to the management of databases and other applications. It contributes to the ability to process, maintain, integrate, secure, audit, and govern other data.”

The concept of metadata is not new and is widely used in the IT industry to define data about data. In ancient times long before the digital age, metadata such as author, title, number of tablets, etc. was already used to catalog collections of clay tablets. As such, metadata provides additional information to better know and use the data.

Metadata Management is the planning, implementation, and control activity that enables access to high-quality, integrated metadata [DMBOK2]. It enhances the data with additional information so that it can be used to:
• Know your data:
◦Reduce uncertainty and possible misinterpretation of the data
◦Know the quality of the data available and associated business rules (data quality business
rules, transformation business rules, etc.)
◦Data origin and usage of the data
◦Improve auditing of Business Intelligence (BI) reports
◦Monitor data volume across the information system to reduce environmental impact
• Manage the data risk and compliance with regulatory requirements:
◦Leverage data classification (confidentiality, privacy) to support data risk management (e.g., to
support data protection impact assessment), base data access model on defined metadata (e.g., roles, responsibility of the user, purpose of data processing, etc.)
◦Leverage security and privacy metadata for the enterprise’s most valuable asset; for example:
▪Security metadata enables the transition from network-centric to attribute-centric security
embodied in new standards such as zero trust that treat data as a corporate asset
▪Enterprise identity management relies on a federated identity (common attributes) to
control human or machine access to data
▪Privacy legislation in many countries and/or groups of countries (e.g., the European Union)
makes the dissemination of personally attributable data illegal
◦Improve auditing of data lineage and usage to meet regulatory requirements
• Manage data lifecycle:
◦Need metadata to indicate what is required to adhere to enterprise policies and directives
◦Need to know what must be archived and retained as a record (often a function of national
legislation)
◦Need to identify retention lifecycle to trigger disposition (deletion)
• Improve time-to-market:
◦For any new business initiative, reduce data scoping effort with the support of good data
documentation (glossary, dictionary, classification)
◦Identify relevant data elements for use cases
• Manage data quality and sharing :
◦Enable information interoperability/sharing to facilitate enterprise and extraprise
collaboration, shared (situational awareness), and decision support
◦Identify redundant and obsolete data
◦Support the business to leverage external data

Metadata is all too often delegated to IT, whereas it is essentially a business concern. Subsequent to numerous investigations in the mid-2000s and new government legislation, metadata is a key corporate asset that has to be maintained to ensure shareholder transparency, corporate security, and client privacy.

The rise of NoSQL databases (relaxed data schemas) and the recent big data trends with the associated promise to unlock value from any kind of data, have led to focus solely on building the capabilities to collect, store, and analyze the data. Very little effort was put on metadata which is often depicted as irrelevant or available automatically using machine learning tools. Beyond market trends, Metadata Management is still a challenge in many organizations for multiple reasons:
• IT complexity:
◦Legacy applications are poorly documented: reference data is lacking, and data changes its
meaning during the lifecycle of the application
◦Mergers and acquisitions are increasing the IT landscape and therefore the scope of metadata
to be documented is changing
◦The replication factor: this concept defines how many times a data element (e.g., customer first
name) is replicated in the information system; the higher the replication factor, the more challenging the metadata documentation effort
• Data complexity:
◦Variety and velocity of data collected (e.g., social media feeds or logs collected near real-time,
text and image collected for machine learning purpose, etc.) require new techniques to collect the relevant metadata
◦Dynamic schemas make it challenging to maintain up-to-date metadata documentation
• IT marketing trends:
◦Microservices/micro applications often challenge data lineage and increase the replication
factor
◦“Agile” delivery is incorrectly interpreted as no requirement for documentation
• Manual work:
◦How to capture the information with business and IT Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs)?
◦What is the right granularity and priority criteria?
◦Metadata validation is not automatic and needs a human review
• Lack of data standards:
◦Naming conventions
◦Data types and unit conventions

However, metadata is key from a business perspective to having good knowledge and understanding of the data already available within the organization. Therefore, metadata is an important foundational data management capacity for any organization looking to efficiently leverage its data.

In the effort to design this capability, we have focused on the minimum set of functions required to effectively deliver Metadata Management. As an organization becomes more mature in the practice, it is possible to go beyond the baseline defined in this framework. We also believe that ethical use of data is becoming more and more important for every organization. It is reflected in the regulations taken in several parts of the world following the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR),[1] which came into force in the EU on May 25, 2018. Even more than compliance to regulatory requirements, it can be a competitive advantage for the organizations that document data usage by design to enable data governance over ethical use of data. Therefore, we have included in this baseline framework “data usage documentation” in the Metadata Management business functions, with an emphasize on personal data.

This section covers the high-level reference model functions and their definitions. More detailed functions are available in the dedicated reference model part of this document in Chapter 5 and Section 5.2.

| 业务术语表文档 | 捕获相关业务概念并分类，以服务数据风险管理（隐私、安全、其他监管要求）。 |

| 数据使用文档 | 维护数据使用方式清单，以满足监管要求。 |

| 数据问题文档 | 记录任何相关业务数据问题（数据质量、主数据、参考数据等）。 |
| 业务资产与技术资产关联 | 为技术元数据提供业务语境。元数据关联提供对数据生命周期的第一层理解：从数据起源，到其在信息系统中经历的各种移动与转换。 |
| 元数据存储库设计 | 把业务需求转化为元数据需求：定义需在元数据存储库中捕获与存储的相关元数据集；定义元数据对象之间应实现的关系与约束；定义在存储库中创建与维护元数据的流程与工作流。 |
| 沟通与培训 | 围绕元数据存储库价值开展沟通；为最终用户（业务与技术）组织培训计划。 |

sections.title_zh: 面向元数据管理能力的 TOGAF 适配
sections.translation_zh:
本章综合元数据管理能力交付语境中应开展的、与 TOGAF ADM 各阶段（预备、A、B、C、D、E、F）相关的关键行动。

| TOGAF ADM 阶段 | 元数据管理建议 |
|---|---|
| 预备阶段 | 确保已识别数据所有者或具有明确元数据业务需求的业务利益相关者，以支持架构工作。确保架构治理委员会与数据治理及运营数据委员会良好整合，以保证架构决策与组织数据战略和数据管理活动一致。确保架构工作产出可在实施阶段通过设计权威机构落地。 |
| A——架构愿景 | 澄清记录元数据的业务驱动因素与将实现的业务目标。捕获元数据管理能力将支持的业务用例、优先级与业务参与者需求。评估组织在元数据管理实践方面的成熟度、现有痛点（如有）与期望改进。形成以下概览：组织内可用元数据源；每个元数据源周围的现有社区（业务与技术参与者）；每个数据源内的元数据生命周期（创建、修改、删除）及各社区相关的元数据管理流程。定义交付业务需求、并依据组织数据战略支持数据治理所需的元数据范围；澄清所需元数据层级、社区与元数据流程集成程度。创建包含概念元数据模型的企业元数据政策。结合业务用例、组织成熟度、现有痛点、可用元数据源与所需集成程度，制定目标元数据管理能力的价值主张。 |
| B——业务架构 | 利用已知监管要求、其他内外部合规要求、业务用例需求、业务数据问题与可用数据集，形式化元数据需求。定义支持业务需求需文档化的关键元数据资产。按元数据范围捕获所需元数据质量水平。识别元数据管理能力的现状（基线）与未来（目标）业务用户、相关角色与访问需求。在数据管理办公室支持下，形式化目标中应实施的组织与详细元数据管理流程。澄清交付业务需求所需的业务功能集，开展基线—目标差距分析；第 5 章的业务参考模型可作为指引（详见 4.2 节）。 |
| C——信息系统架构 | 把概念元数据模型扩展到逻辑层（规定属性与域），再把概念元数据实体/属性映射到逻辑数据模型实体、记录（元组/实例）或属性。定义元数据集成模型，澄清：目标元数据存储库（支持数据治理）所管理元数据范围；目标存储库与组织内现有元数据源之间的主/次角色；目标存储库与其他元数据源之间元数据交换的协作契约。定义目标中相关的元数据采集方式：手工摄取、从源推送、从源拉取。澄清元数据推断需求（如有）及推断复杂度——数据多样性（结构化、半结构化、非结构化）与 IT 架构是两大影响因素。数据文档化的关键挑战之一，是记录数据从其起源、到在信息系统中经历的移动与转换的生命周期；这通过元数据关联实现，通常需要人工投入，因此应基于业务需求澄清关联范围，集中精力。澄清交付业务需求所需的应用功能集，开展基线—目标差距分析（5.2 节应用参考模型可作指引，详见 4.3 节）。 |
| D——技术架构 | 元数据 IT 能力的完整覆盖可能需要多种技术组合：数据集成厂商通常提供优化连接器，从数据集成存储库、数据库字典及半结构化/非结构化数据模式中抽取技术与运营元数据；数据治理方案较少聚焦技术元数据抽取，但提供治理功能（元数据变更校验工作流、合规报表等）。定义交付元数据管理能力需要一种技术还是技术组合。确保信息交换平台服务在企业内外每次交换中都包含相关元数据——这对来自外部供应商和/或伙伴的入站数据尤为重要。 |
| E——机会与解决方案 | 使用应用参考模型审视解决方案供应商的方案（原文“provided in Section”未写出节号）。 |
| F——迁移规划 | 首先，在电子表格中开始记录元数据资产，聚焦小范围，以熟悉概念并在团队内培育文档文化。元数据文档需要人工投入：业务元数据由人管理，技术元数据存在于 IT 系统数据结构中，运营元数据在特定时点生成。这一阶段还应证明记录元数据的价值。下一步，迁移到集中式存储库，以执行元数据治理（管家职责、所有权、校验工作流等）、扩展文档规模、简化元数据访问与管理。集中式存储库有多项好处：把不同利益相关者（业务数据所有者、数据管家、内控人员、数据保护官、数据经理等）纳入同一存储库，便于知识共享与复用；所有资产已集中于一个存储库，便于元数据关联；集中式元数据管理支持元数据治理。但由数据管理办公室执行的强治理模型、以及各利益相关者的接纳可能颇具挑战，因为存储库未必针对其角色与特定需求。随着各方成熟，可能出现更高级需求（自动数据发现（例如记录链接）与编目、数据流可视化、数据模式自动逆向工程等）；此时可考虑为不同贡献者群体设立专用存储库，即按逻辑资产组定义专用系统（业务术语表库、数据字典库、数据质量规则文档与实施库等），从而为每类元数据文档功能提供高级特性，并为每个角色定制界面；但需投入专用精力做元数据集成，把资产关联起来、确保各库一致、避免孤岛，且不同利益相关者之间的协作可能受限。 |
| G——实施治理 | 与元数据管理项目（存储库实施、元数据集成）组织合规审查，检查其遵循原则与目标架构。 |

source_units.text_en: 4.1. TOGAF Adaptation for a Metadata Management
Capability
This chapter describes a synthesis of key actions related to the TOGAF ADM phases (Preliminary, A, B, C, D, E, F) that should be performed in the context of a Metadata Management capability delivery.

| TOGAF ADM Phase | Metadata Management Recommendation | | --- | --- | | Preliminary Phase | Make sure that the data owners or any business stakeholders with clear metadata business
requirements are identified to support the architecture work.
Make sure that there is an architecture governance board well integrated with other data
governance and operational data boards. This is to ensure that the architecture decisions are
consistent with the organization data strategy and data management activities.
Ensure that the outputs of the architecture work can be operationalized during the
implementation phase via a design authority. | | Phase A:
Architecture Vision | Clarify the business drivers to document metadata and the business goals that will be
achieved.
Capture the business use cases that will be supported by the Metadata Management capability,
the priorities, and the business actor requirements.
Assess the maturity of the organization in relation to Metadata Management practice, existing
pain points if any, and expected improvements.
Develop an overview of:
• The metadata sources available within the organization
• The existing communities (business and technical actors) around each metadata source
• The metadata lifecycle (create, modify, delete) within each source and related Metadata
Management processes of each community
Define the scope of metadata required to deliver the business requirements and to support
data governance in accordance with the organization’s data strategy. Clarify the level of
metadata, community, and metadata process integration required.
Create an enterprise metadata policy including a conceptual metadata model.
Develop the value proposition of the target Metadata Management capability taking into
consideration the business use cases, organization maturity, existing pain points, metadata
sources available, and the level of integration required. |

| TOGAF ADM Phase | Metadata Management Recommendation | | --- | --- | | Phase B:
Business Architecture | Leverage known regulatory requirements, other internal and external compliance
requirements, business use case requirements, business data issues, and available data sets to
formalize metadata requirements.
Define key metadata assets to be documented to support the business requirements.
Capture the level of metadata quality required per scope of metadata.
Identify the as-is (baseline) and to-be (target) business users of the Metadata Management
capability, the related roles, and access requirements.
Formalize the organization and detailed Metadata Management processes that should be
implemented in the target with the support of the Data Management Office.
Clarify the set of business functions that are required to deliver the business requirements and
perform the baseline versus target gap analysis. The business reference model provided in
Chapter 5 can be used as a guide for this step.
Refer to Section 4.2 for further details about the metadata requirements, the metadata model,
and Metadata Management processes. |

| TOGAF ADM Phase | Metadata Management Recommendation | | --- | --- | | Phase C:
Information Systems
Architectures | Extend the conceptual metadata model into the logical level (attributes and domains specified)
and then map the conceptual metadata entities or attributes to the logical data model entities,
records (tuples/instances), or attributes.
Define the metadata integration model, clarifying:
• The scope of metadata that is managed within the target metadata repository that will
support data governance
• Primary/secondary roles between the target metadata repository and the existing
metadata sources within the organization
• The collaboration contract for metadata exchange between the target repository and other
sources of metadata
Define the metadata collection approach that is relevant in the target: manual ingestion,
pushing metadata from sources, pulling metadata from sources.
Clarify the metadata inference requirements (if any) and the level of complexity pertaining to
this inference. Data variety (structured, semi-structured, unstructured) and IT landscape are
two important factors of metadata inference complexity.
One of the key challenges about data documentation is to document the data lifecycle from its
origin as well as the movements and transformations it has been through in the information
systems. This is done through metadata associations and typically requires manual effort.
Therefore, clarify metadata association requirements based on business requirements to
concentrate the effort on the relevant scope.
Clarify the set of application functions that are required to deliver the business requirements
and perform the baseline versus target gap analysis. The application reference model provided
in Section 5.2 can be used as a guide for this step.
Refer to Section 4.3 for more details about this step. | | Phase D:
Technology
Architecture | Full coverage of the metadata IT capability may require multiple technologies to be combined.
Data integration vendors in general provide optimized connectors to extract the technical and
operational metadata from data integration repositories, database dictionaries, and data
patterns inside semi-structured and unstructured data. Data governance solutions are less
focused on technical metadata extraction, but provide functions for governance such as
metadata change validation workflow, compliance reporting, etc.
Define whether a technology or a combination of technologies is required to deliver the
Metadata Management capability.
Ensure that the information exchange platform services include the relevant metadata for
every exchange internal and external to the enterprise. This is particularly important to
incoming data from external vendors and/or partners. | | Phase E:
Opportunities &
Solutions | Use the application reference model provided in Section to challenge solution providers. |

| TOGAF ADM Phase | Metadata Management Recommendation | | --- | --- | | Phase F:
Migration Planning | First, start documenting the metadata assets in a spreadsheet focusing on a small scope to
become familiar with the concepts and foster a documentation culture within the team.
Metadata documentation requires manual effort: business metadata is managed by people,
technical metadata exists in the data structures of the IT systems, operational metadata is
generated at a specific point in time. This first step should also aim to prove the value of
documenting metadata.
Next, move to a centralized repository to enforce metadata governance (stewardship,
ownership, validation workflow, etc.), scale metadata documentation, and ease metadata
access and administration management. A centralized repository has several benefits, such as
the ease of knowledge sharing and re-use by bringing the different stakeholders (business data
owner, data steward, internal controllers, data protection officer, data manager, etc.) into the
same repository, the ease of metadata association as all the assets are already collected into a
single repository, and the centralized metadata stewardship to support metadata governance.
However, a strong governance model enforced by the Data Management Office and the
onboarding of the different stakeholders (business data owner, data steward, internal
controllers, data protection officer, data manager, etc.) can be challenging as the repository
may not be dedicated to their role and specific needs.
The more mature the different stakeholders become, the more advanced requirements might
emerge such as automated data discovery (e.g., record linkage) and catalog, data flow
visualization, automated reverse engineering of data schemas, etc. At this stage, it can make
sense to consider dedicated repositories for different families of contributors to support their
specific requirements. This means that a dedicated system can be defined per logical group of
assets. For example, a repository for a business glossary, a repository for data dictionaries, a
repository for data quality rules documentation and implementation, etc. It is therefore
possible to provide advanced features dedicated to each metadata documentation function and
to support specific user interfaces customized for each role or family of users. However, a
dedicated effort should be put into metadata integration to link the metadata assets together,
ensure consistency between the repositories, and avoid silos. Also, collaboration between the
different stakeholders can be limited. | | Phase G:
Implementation
Governance | Organize a compliance review with Metadata Management projects (metadata repository
implementation, metadata integration) to check that they respect the principles and target
architecture. |

元数据在组织内有多个来源（图 4-1）。主要挑战在于把不同种类、来自不同社区、具有不同流程与生命周期的元数据汇聚起来，以实现特定业务目标，如数据合规、数据质量监控与数据可访问性。

source_units.text_en: 4.2. Metadata Management Guidelines for a Business
Architecture (ADM Phase B)

Metadata is available in multiple sources within an organization; see Figure 4-1. The main challenge is to bring together different kinds of metadata, from different communities, with different processes and lifecycles, in order to achieve specific business goals such as data compliance, data quality monitoring, and data accessibility.
Figure 4-1: Metadata Sources Illustration
(Metadata domains have been harvested from use cases and applied to the context of this document.)

Our recommendation is to engage in a step-by-step progressive approach to build the metadata documentation rather than attempt to document all the assets identified in the existing metadata sources at the same time.

sections.translation_zh:
定义元数据需求有不同方法（图 4-2）：

- **自上而下**：从合规或其他业务用例出发形式化元数据需求，例如：
  - 合规：法规（GDPR、偿付能力 II、IFRS 17）、内部（数字可持续性、安全规则）；
  - 业务用例：获取客户交互数据以改进向上销售。
- **自下而上**：基于业务数据问题或数据集需求，例如：
  - 数据集：为支持 BI 与分析用例，对现有客户信息文件（CIF）进行文档化；
  - 业务数据问题：客户被以错误频率开票，导致不满与投诉；调查根因以解决问题。



自上而下方法（合规、业务用例）通常有强有力的业务支持，元数据一致性由校验流程与工作流要求并保障。自下而上方法更具机会主义色彩，未必有强业务支持；采用该方法时，重要的是在进一步自动化与治理前用具体例子展示价值。两种情况下，都应澄清元数据需求，包括期望的元数据质量水平。

图4-2：元数据需求收集示意。

source_units.text_en: 4.2.1. Collect Metadata Requirements
There are different approaches to define metadata requirements (see Figure 4-2):
• A top-down approach starting with compliance or other business use cases to formalize metadata requirements; for example:
◦Compliance: Regulation (GDPR, Solvency II,[1] IFRS 17[2]), internal (digital sustainability, security
rules)
◦Business use cases: get customer interactions data to improve up-sell
• A bottom-up approach based on business data issues or data set requirements; for example:
◦Data set: document existing Customer Information File (CIF) to support BI & Analytics use cases
◦Business data issue: customers are invoiced at the wrong frequency generating frustrations and
complaints; investigate root causes to tackle the issue
Figure 4-2: Metadata Requirements Collection Illustration

The top-down approach (compliance, business use cases) often has strong business support; metadata consistency is required and guaranteed by validation processes and workflows. The bottom-up approach is more opportunistic and does not always have strong business support. For this approach it is important to show the value with concrete examples before further automation and governance. In both cases, it is important to clarify the metadata requirements including the expected level of metadata quality required.

semantic_rules.statement_zh: 自上而下和自下而上都需明确元数据及预期质量要求。
semantic_rules.boundary_zh: 前者通常业务支持强，后者先以具体价值证明支持；不是互斥方法。

sections.title_zh: 形式化元数据管理流程
sections.translation_zh:
元数据质量由流程与校验工作流保障，可因元数据范围而异。主要有两种方法（图 4-3）：

- **规范式**：旨在保证元数据的精确、准确、完整与一致。元数据由少数人创建、以只读方式发布、静态（随时间变化少），其生命周期通过校验工作流管理；适合受监管约束、集中管理的元数据。
- **协作式**：更适合数据民主化场景——需要多个贡献者维护技术元数据，并在需要时把技术元数据与业务元数据关联以提供业务语境；多人创建、多人编辑、动态、最终一致。

图4-3：元数据质量保障方法。

source_units.text_en: 4.2.2. Formalize Metadata Management Processes
Metadata quality is enforced by processes and validation workflows that can vary per metadata scope. There are mainly two approaches (see Figure 4-3):
• The normative approach, which aims to guarantee precision, accuracy, integrity, and consistency of the metadata

In this approach the metadata is created by a few, published as read-only, static (few changes overtime), and its lifecycle is managed via validation workflows. It fits well with metadata subject to regulatory constraints and central organization.

• The collaborative approach is more appropriate in the data democratization approach where there is a need to have multiple contributors maintaining the technical metadata and, when required, to associate the technical metadata with business metadata to provide a business context: created by many, edited by many, dynamic, eventual consistency
Figure 4-3: Metadata Quality Enforcement Approaches

semantic_rules.statement_zh: 协作式允许多人维护、动态及最终一致以支持数据民主化。
semantic_rules.boundary_zh: 最终一致不是无需质量条件或无需治理。

sections.title_en: 4.3. Metadata Management Guidelines for Information Systems Architectures (ADM Phase C)
sections.title_zh: 信息系统架构阶段的元数据管理指南（ADM 阶段 C）
sections.translation_zh:
元数据存储库由元数据管理 IT 方案支撑。该方案是技术（功能集）、数据模型与流程（元数据更新与校验工作流）的组合，用于支持元数据管理活动。





元数据数据模型通过澄清将在元数据存储库中记录的元数据资产集合及其关系，把元数据需求形式化。如 4.2 节所述，元数据校验工作流的设计旨在满足元数据质量需求。

参照 DMBOK2，元数据通常分为三类：

- **业务元数据**：主要关注数据的内容与状况，并包含与数据治理相关的细节。
- **技术元数据**：提供有关数据的技术细节、存储数据的系统，以及在系统内部和系统之间移动数据的流程的信息。
- **运营元数据**：描述数据被处理和访问的细节。

业务元数据由人管理，技术元数据存在于 IT 系统的数据结构中，运营元数据在特定时点生成。图 4-5 给出了为支持数据治理而应捕获的关键元数据资产的基线建议（定义见附录 A）。





确定要记录的元数据资产后，重要的是在属性层面利用都柏林核心™ 元数据元素集（Dublin Core™ Metadata Element Set，DCMES）[DCMES] 来有效描述每项资产。例如，subject（主题）字段对于确保元数据在整个企业内可被普遍发现至关重要。让标签与逻辑数据模型元素（尤其是泛化—特化构造，例如“轿车是一种汽车，汽车是一种交通工具”）相对应（映射）很有用，这样搜索（以及业务规则）就能为任何目的找到所有必需的数据。

一旦要收集的元数据资产范围确定，就需要澄清元数据集成模型，同时考虑现有元数据源的更大范围，以及业务架构产出（要接入的业务参与者、元数据校验流程、数据治理运营模式）。

如 ISO/IEC 19773 所述：“……它是一个适用于任何组织中任何种类数据、服务于任何目的的通用描述框架。ISO/IEC 19773 不涉及其他数据管理需求，例如数据模型、应用规格、程序代码、项目群计划、业务计划和业务政策。”[ISO/IEC 19773]

此处提出的框架旨在超越 ISO/IEC 19773 模型，明确既与支持数据语义文档相关、又与数据管理需求相关的关键资产。

表 4-1 展示了观察到的三种常见模型及其影响。

**表 4-1：元数据集成模型示例**

| 元数据集成模型 | 说明与影响 |
|---|---|
| 汇集式（Consolidation） | 元数据存储库提供唯一的访问点，用于消费来自不同来源的可用元数据。它仅保存业务元数据的副本。创建和维护这些元数据的流程位于存储库之外。 |
| 混合式（Hybrid） | 对于一部分元数据，由存储库保存主副本。存储库还设计为支持维护这些元数据所需的流程与校验工作流。现有工具预计在迁移到元数据存储库后退役。对于其余元数据范围，由现有工具保存主副本，并与元数据存储库同步。 |
| 统一式（Unified） | 存储库在完整范围内统一，既统一元数据，也统一维护元数据所需的流程与校验工作流。还可以努力根据各用户社区的需求为其提供专属用户体验，这可能涉及专属用户界面。 |













元数据交换可通过以下方式之一完成：

- **手工摄取（Manual ingestion）**：每个来源以约定格式导出元数据，再手工上传到存储库。
- **推送元数据（Pushing metadata）**：每个来源负责按协作契约（格式、数据结构、频率等）把约定范围内的元数据推送到元数据存储库。
- **拉取元数据（Pulling metadata）**：支撑元数据存储库的 IT 方案提供元数据代理，可直接部署在来源端以收集或推断元数据。

技术元数据与运营元数据通常采用拉取方式；业务元数据则需要人工投入。





每种方式都有一些需要考虑的影响：

- **手工摄取**：
  - 人工工作会影响运营效率；
  - 供应商对元数据集成的支持可能有限；
  - 需要初始投入，为每个元数据源构建抽取器。
- **推送元数据**：
  - 需要初始投入，为每个元数据源设置抽取器；
  - 可能需要额外工具来支持元数据集成。
- **拉取元数据**：
  - 元数据解决方案可能有权访问所有数据；事实上，工具有时需要访问数据文件才能推断技术元数据；
  - 元数据代理对关键应用而言可能是一个侵入性组件；
  - 由于元数据解决方案将拥有对信息系统全景中多个应用的读访问权限，因此需要开展安全审计，确保符合安全政策。

收集技术与运营元数据的复杂性取决于数据多样性和 IT 全景。主要差异在于：数据模式与运营元数据是“按设计”定义，还是事后借助分析技术（元数据推断、机器学习等）提取。





- 结构化数据可以很容易地从数据库字典、技术元数据存储、数据集成存储库等收集。
  注意，收集数据模式不需要访问数据。
- 半结构化文件带有结构，但不能保证模式随时间保持稳定，因为每个文件可能有自己的结构。
- 非结构化数据：我们无法管理自己不知道的内容。
  在分析和治理之前，必须从非结构化数据中提取最低限度的结构（图像中的形状、文档中的电子邮件地址等）。这项工作需要扫描数据内容；如果要扫描数百万个文件，可能涉及密集的数据处理。

存在多种技术、库或工具可从数据中提取技术与运营元数据；工具选择取决于所需元数据的种类、提取信息的复杂性，以及待扫描数据的性能与数据量。

在某种程度上，管理非结构化数据的元数据意味着首先要捕获技术元数据；同一非结构化数据集可以随时间提取出多种结构。主要挑战在于维护与其他元数据的关联，从而把这部分非结构化数据置于语境中：

- **业务含义**：与业务术语、业务数据对象、业务数据元素关联；
- **使用语境**：与数据处理活动关联；
- **数据质量要求**：与业务数据质量规则、技术数据质量规则、数据质量异常关联；
- **隐私要求**：与数据删除规则等关联。

source_units.text_en: 4.3. Metadata Management Guidelines for Information
Systems Architectures (ADM Phase C)

The metadata repository is supported by a Metadata Management IT solution, which is a combination of technologies (set of functions), a data model, and processes (metadata update and validation workflows) in order to support Metadata Management activities.
Figure 4-4: Metadata Management IT Solution

The metadata data model formalizes the metadata requirements by clarifying the set of metadata assets that will be documented in the metadata repository and their relationships. As described in Section 4.2, the metadata validation workflows are designed to support metadata quality requirements.
Metadata is often divided into three categories that can be summarized as follows, based on the DMBOK2:
• Business metadata focuses largely on the content and condition of the data and includes details related to data governance
• Technical metadata provides information about the technical details of data, the systems that store data, and the processes that move it within and between systems
• Operational metadata describes details of the processing and accessing of data

Business metadata is managed by people, technical metadata exists in the data structures of the IT systems, and operational metadata is generated at a specific point in time. Figure 4-5 shows a baseline proposal of key metadata assets (see the definitions in Appendix A) to be captured to support data governance.
Figure 4-5: Key Metadata Assets

After identifying the metadata data assets to be documented, it is important to leverage the Dublin Core™ Metadata Element Set (DCMES) [DCMES] at the attribute level to effectively describe each asset. For instance, the subject field is key to making sure that metadata is universally discoverable throughout the enterprise. It is useful to have the tags correspond (map) to the logical data model elements, especially the generalization-specialization constructs (e.g., Sedan is a type of Car that is a type of vehicle) so that searches (and business rules) can find all of the requisite data for whatever purpose.

Once the scope of metadata assets to be collected is defined, the metadata integration model needs to be clarified taking into consideration the broader scope of existing metadata sources and the business architecture outputs (business actors to be onboarded, metadata validation processes, data governance operating model).

As stated in ISO/IEC 19773, “… it is a general description framework for data of any kind, in any organization, and for any purpose. ISO/IEC 19773 does not address other data management needs, such as data models, application specifications, programming code, program plans, business plans, and business policies.” [ISO/IEC 19773]
The proposed framework here is to go beyond the ISO/IEC 19773 model by making explicit the key assets that are relevant to support data semantics documentation but also data management needs.

The metadata exchange can be done by one of the following:
• Manual ingestion: Each source exports the metadata in the agreed format and it is uploaded manually in the repository
• Pushing metadata: Each source takes the responsibility to push to the metadata repository an agreed scope according to the collaboration contract (format, data structure, frequency, etc.)
• Pulling metadata: The IT solution supporting the metadata repository provides metadata agents that can be deployed directly at source to collect or infer the metadata
This is usually the case for technical and operational metadata. Business metadata requires manual effort.
Figure 4-9: Metadata Integration Patterns
Each approach has some implications to be taken into consideration:
• Manual ingestion:
◦Manual work with an impact on operational efficiency
◦Possible limited vendor support to metadata integration
◦Initial effort to build the extractors for each metadata source
• Pushing metadata:
◦Initial effort to set up the extractors for each metadata source
◦Possible additional tool(s) required to support metadata integration
• Pulling metadata:
◦The metadata solution may have access to all the data; indeed, sometimes the tool will have
access to the data files to be able to infer the technical metadata
◦The metadata agent can be an intrusive component for critical applications
◦Security audit is required to ensure compliance with security policies as the metadata solution
will have read access to multiple applications in the information system landscape

The complexity to collect technical and operational metadata depends on the data variety and IT landscape, with a main difference when the data schema and operational metadata are defined by- design versus when the metadata is extracted a posteriori by leveraging analytical techniques (metadata inference, machine learning, etc.).
Figure 4-10: Technical Metadata Inference
• Structured data can be easily collected from database dictionaries, technical metadata stores, data integration repositories, etc.
Note that data schema collection does not require access to data.
• Semi-structured files come with a structure but do not guarantee schema stability over time as each file may have its own structure
• Unstructured data: we cannot manage what we do not know

A minimum structure (shapes in an image; email address from a document, etc.) must be extracted from the unstructured data before analysis and governance. Such an exercise requires scanning the data content which may involve intensive data processing if there are millions of files to scan.

Multiple techniques/libraries/tools exist to extract technical and operational metadata from data; the tool selection depends on the kind of metadata that is needed, the complexity to extract the information, and the performance/volume of data to scan.

To a certain extent, managing metadata for unstructured data means first capturing the technical metadata; multiple structures can be extracted over time from the same unstructured data set. The main challenge is to maintain the associations with other metadata to put this unstructured data in context:
• Business meaning: association with the business terms, business data objects, business data elements
• Context of use: association with data processing activities
• Data quality requirement: association with business data quality rule, technical data quality rule, data quality anomaly
• Privacy requirement: association with data deletion rule, etc.

| 类别 | 名称 | 定义 | |---|---|---| | 业务 | 活动（Activity） | 业务为达成明确目标而开展的一项业务任务或一组业务任务。（来源：集成架构框架（IAF）） | | 业务 | 业务数据删除规则（Business Data Deletion Rule） | 关于移除一组业务数据元素的业务规则，可执行以满足监管或业务要求。通常由业务数据所有者作为其数据治理职责的一部分，为其拥有的数据域定义数据删除规则。定义这些规则时应征求其他数据参与者（业务数据所有者、数据管家、内部控制人员、数据保护官、数据经理等）的意见。这些规则是合乎伦理地使用数据的关键组成部分，并能与数据提供方和消费方建立信任。 | | 业务 | 业务数据域（Business Data Domain） | 一个主题域、一个业务领域以及（在相关时）其他维度（如地理区域、组织）的组合，构成用于数据治理目的的数据和/或元数据的一致分组。细粒度数据域通常聚焦数据治理（如负责理赔数据质量的数据域）或高度特定的元数据（如仅在受限语境中才有意义的一个数据元素或数据质量规则）。宏观层面定义的数据域通常聚焦共享元数据的治理（如在整个企业广泛使用的一个数据元素或数据质量规则）。 | | 业务 | 业务数据元素（Business Data Element） | 基本的概念性数据单元。“变量”和“字段”常被同义使用，表示数据元素（如个人合同状态、理赔事件日期、员工名字）。数据元素由三个部分组成：数据对象——所关注并被描述的想法、人或事物（如客户）；属性——数据对象中令人关注的特性（如客户首选语言）；值域——确定可用于表示该数据元素的允许值。

值域具有数据类型（如布尔、十进制、整数），并可选地具有最小长度、最大长度和小数精度。值域可以是枚举的（通过至少两个单独允许值的列表指定）或非枚举的。例如，客户首选语言由语言代码列表 [ISO 639-1] 表示。数据元素可分为以下组之一：
• 输入型：若数据元素为输入型，表示数据基本上按采集时的样子使用或存储，未经重大修改；大多数数据元素属于此类
• 派生型：一个或多个数据元素以某种方式被修改；例如，多个数据元素可能为输出或逻辑目的聚合在一起

更多信息见表 5-1。 | | 业务 | 业务数据问题（Business Data Issue） | 描述因数据问题而产生的业务问题及该问题的影响（定性或定量）。还描述业务影响的性质，如财务、监管、法律、声誉、运营等。 | | 业务 | 业务数据对象（Business Data Object） | 为企业所采集数据提供语境的关键想法、人或事物。数据对象有助于理解，并可用于定义收集多个数据元素所针对的对象。例如，可将“联系”定义为数据对象，这有助于应用数据元素，包括联系日期、联系交付方式、联系客户在场状态。使用数据对象可减少在多个数据元素中重复大段文本。 | | 业务 | 业务数据质量规则（Business Data Quality Rule） | 与一个业务数据元素或一组业务数据元素相关的业务规则，可通过测试确定这些业务数据元素是否满足数据质量要求。通常由业务数据所有者作为其数据治理职责的一部分，为其拥有的数据域定义数据质量规则。定义数据质量规则时应征求其他数据参与者（业务数据所有者、数据管家、内部控制人员、数据保护官、数据经理等）的意见。数据质量规则的定义、设计与实施是稳健数据质量管理项目群的核心。示例：出生日期必须是有效日期；姓氏不得为空；电子邮件地址必须匹配 user@domain 模式。 | | 业务 | 业务规则（Business Rule） | 可实施且属于业务管辖范围的规则。源自业务政策。（来源：对象管理组（OMG）） | | 业务 | 业务术语（Business Term） | 用于描述事物、以语言或业务分支表达概念的词或短语。 | | 业务 | 代码集（Code Set） | 定义一组值，枚举数据元素的可能值。例如，可为业务数据对象“人”的业务数据元素“性别”定义代码集，可能值为：男、女、未知。 | | 业务 | 代码值（Code Value） | 代码集的一个实例或单个值。 | | 业务 | 数据分类体系（Data Classification Taxonomies） | 数据文档化的一项重要活动，需要至少四类专业群体协作：信息安全、数据隐私、信息风险管理和数据管理。因此，它会影响安全措施、对个人与敏感数据的监管约束，以及数据管理与质量优先级。随着 GDPR 等监管要求的出现，其重要性日益提高。数据分类体系是应用于对每个数据元素分类的适用标签。尽管它们本质上是代码集与代码值，我们仍选择突出数据分类体系，因为它们需要多个利益相关者之间达成一致。 | | 业务 | 数据政策（Data Policy） | 适用于数据的一组规则、指南、标准与模式。 | | 业务 | 数据隐私评估（Data Privacy Assessment） | 一项旨在识别与个人数据使用相关风险、并定义缓解计划以符合监管要求的过程。 | | 业务 | 数据处理活动（Data Processing Activity） | 为产生有意义的信息而对数据元素进行的收集与操作。它表示对数据或数据集执行的任何操作或系列操作，无论是否采用自动化手段（原文为“whether by automated means”，表述不完整），例如收集、记录、组织、结构化、存储、改编或变更、检索、咨询、使用、经传输披露、传播或以其他方式提供、对齐或组合、限制、擦除或销毁。在 GDPR 语境中，数据处理活动记录是收集和操作个人数据的那部分数据处理活动。 | | 业务 | 组织（Organization） | 用于描述公司内由共同目的界定的利益相关者群体。通常描述分支机构、部门、团队等组织单元。用于驱动元数据存储库内的运营治理。在某些语境中，可能需要按组织单元细分业务数据域。 | | 业务 | 流程（Process） | 一组相互关联或相互作用的活动，利用输入交付预期结果 [ISO 9000]。 | | 业务 | 角色（Role） | 业务角色是执行特定行为的职责，可将参与者分配给该角色，或代表参与者在特定行动或事件中所扮演的部分。（来源：ArchiMate 规范） | | 业务 | 服务水平协议（SLAs） | 运营数据治理的关键组成部分。它们在每个业务语境中描述支持业务用例所需的适用服务水平。例如，针对个人电子邮件地址的数据质量规则可能因业务运营模式（B2C 或 B2B2C）而有不同的可接受阈值。在第二种情形（B2B2C）中，如果公司与客户没有直接关系，电子邮件地址的质量可能无关紧要。 | | 运营 | 数据访问事件（Data Access Event） | 信息系统中记录的、用于跟踪用户账户对某数据子集访问的任何事件。 | | 运营 | 数据质量异常（Data Quality Anomaly） | 在信息系统内执行技术数据质量规则后检测到的问题。 | | 运营 | 数据量（Data Volume） | 数据集或数据库中数据数量的度量。 | | 运营 | 元数据活动日志（Metadata Activity Logs） | 与元数据存储库内开展的任何活动相关的一组事件。 | | 技术 | 应用（Application） | 为执行特定任务（如文字处理、数据库管理或图形处理）而设计的一类计算机程序。 | | 技术 | 数据流（Data Flow） | 描述应用之间的数据流。 | | 技术 | 数据库（Database） | 有组织的数据集合，通常以电子方式从计算机系统存储和访问。数据库管理系统（DBMS）是与最终用户、应用及数据库本身交互以捕获和分析数据的软件。（来源：维基百科） | | 技术 | 数据字段（Data Field） | 可存储数据的位置。通常指数据库中的列，或数据录入表单/Web 表单中的字段。（来源：维基百科） | | 技术 | 数据集（Data Set） | 一组相关的离散数据项，可单独访问、组合访问或作为一个整体实体管理。（来源：TechTarget） | | 技术 | 技术数据删除规则（Technical Data Deletion Rule） | 业务数据删除规则描述的物理可执行组件（多数情况下为 SQL SELECT 语句）。IT 负责设计并开发数据删除规则，之后可在全企业的批处理或近实时应用中实施、执行与监控。数据删除规则的输出是不符合该规则的所有业务引用列表（如合同引用/编号、员工引用/编号、供应商引用/编号等）（例如，不应保留在 BI 与分析平台中的所有客户联系详情列表）。 | | 技术 | 技术数据质量规则（Technical Data Quality Rule） | 业务数据质量规则的物理可执行组件。IT 负责设计并开发数据质量规则，之后可在全企业的批处理或近实时应用中实施、执行与监控。数据质量规则的输出是不符合该规则的所有业务引用列表（如合同引用/编号、员工引用/编号、供应商引用/编号等）（例如，合同开始日期不是有效日期的所有合同引用列表）。 |

source_units.text_en: A: Metadata Asset Definitions

| Category | Name | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | Business | Activity | A business task or group of business tasks that are undertaken by the
business to achieve a well-defined goal. (Source: Integrated Architecture
Framework (IAF)) | | Business | Business Data Deletion Rule | A business rule related to the removal of a set of business data elements
that can be executed to meet regulatory or business requirements. It is
typically the responsibility of business data owners, as part of their
data governance responsibilities, to define data deletion rules for the
data domains they own. They should seek input from other data actors
(business data owner, data steward, internal controllers, data
protection officer, data manager, etc.) as they define these rules.
These are an essential component for an ethical use of the data and
build trust with the data providers and consumers. | | Business | Business Data Domain | A combination of one subject area, one business area, and (when
relevant) other dimensions (e.g., geographical area, organization) that
constitutes a consistent grouping of data and/or metadata for data
governance purposes. Fine-grained data domains usually focus on
governance of data (e.g., the data domain in charge of the data quality
of a claim) or highly specific metadata (e.g., one data element or data
quality rule that makes sense in a restricted context). Data domains
defined at macro level usually focus on governance of shared metadata
(e.g., one data element or data quality rule that is widely used around
the enterprise). |

| Category | Name | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | Business | Business Data Element | A fundamental, conceptual unit of data. Often, the terms “variable” and
“field” are used synonymously to mean a data element (e.g., Individual
Contract Status, Claim Event Date, and Employee First Name). A data
element is comprised of three components:
• A data object – the idea, person, or thing that is of interest and is
being described (e.g., the Customer)
• A property – the property is the characteristic of the data object
that is of interest (e.g., Customer Preferred Language)
• A value domain – establishes the permissible values that can be
used to represent the data element
A value domain has a data type (e.g., boolean, decimal, and integer)
and, optionally, a minimum length, a maximum length, and a decimal
precision. A value domain can be enumerated (specified through a list
of values of a least two individual permissible values) or non-
enumerated. For example, the Customer Preferred Language is
represented by a list of language codes [ISO 639-1]. Data elements can
be thought of as belonging to one of the following groups:
• Input: if a data element is of the input type, this indicates that the
data is used or stored essentially as it is collected, without major
modification; most data elements are of this type
• Derived: one or more data elements which are modified in some
way; for example, multiple data elements might be aggregated
together for output or logical purposes
See Table 5-1 for more information. | | Business | Business Data Issue | Describes a business problem occurring as the result of a data issue and
the impact of this problem, either qualitative or quantitative. Also
describes the nature of the business impact such as financial,
regulatory, legal, reputational, operational, etc. | | Business | Business Data Object | A key idea, person, or thing that provides context for the data collected
through the enterprise. Data objects aid understanding and are useful
for defining objects against which multiple data elements are collected.
For example, “contact” may be defined as a data object, which aids in
the application of data elements, including contact date, contact
delivery mode, and contact customer present status. The use of data
objects reduces the repetition of large sections of text across multiple
data elements. |

| Category | Name | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | Business | Business Data Quality Rule | A business rule related to a business data element or a set of business
data elements that can be tested to determine if the business data
elements meet the data quality requirements. It is typically the
responsibility of business data owners, as part of their data governance
responsibilities, to define data quality rules for data domains they own.
They should seek input from other data actors (business data owner,
data steward, internal controllers, data protection officer, data
manager, etc.) as they define the data quality rules. The definition,
design, and implementation of data quality rules are at the heart of a
solid data quality management program.
Examples: Date of Birth must be a valid date. Surname must not be
empty. Email address must match patternuser@domain. | | Business | Business Rule | A rule that is practicable and that is under business jurisdiction.
Derived from business policy. (Source: Object Management Group
(OMG)) | | Business | Business Term | Words or phrases used to describe a thing to express a concept in
language or branch of business. | | Business | Code Set | Defines a list of values that enumerate the possible values for a data
element. We can, for instance, define a code set for the business data
element “Gender” of the business data object “Person” with the
following possible values: male, female, unknown. | | Business | Code Value | An instance or a single value of a code set. | | Business | Data Classification
Taxonomies | An important activity of the data documentation which requires
collaboration between at least four professional groups: Information
Security, Data Privacy, Information Risk Management, and Data
Management. Consequently, it has impacts on security measures, on
regulatory constraints on personal and sensitive data, and on data
management and quality priorities. It has increased in importance
following regulatory requirements such as GDPR. Data classification
taxonomies are applicable labels that should be used to classify each
data element. Even if they are essentially code set and code values, we
have chosen to highlight data classifications taxonomies as they require
alignment between multiple stakeholders. | | Business | Data Policy | A set of rules, guidelines, standards, and patterns that are applied to the
data. | | Business | Data Privacy Assessment | A process designed to identify risks related to the use of personal data
and define mitigation plans to be compliant with regulatory
requirements. |

| Category | Name | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | Business | Data Processing Activity | The collection and manipulation of data elements to produce
meaningful information. It represents any operation or set of
operations which is performed on data or on sets of data, whether by
automated means, such as collection, recording, organization,
structuring, storage, adaptation or alteration, retrieval, consultation,
use, disclosure by transmission, dissemination or otherwise making
available, alignment or combination, restriction, erasure or destruction.
In the context of GDPR, the record of data processing activities is the
subset of data processing activities which collect and manipulate
personal data. | | Business | Organization | Used to describe a group of stakeholders within the company that are
bounded by a common purpose. It often describes organizational units
such as branches, departments, teams, etc.
Used to animate the operational governance within the metadata
repository. It may be required in some context to specialize the business
data domain per organization units. | | Business | Process | A set of interrelated or interacting activities that use inputs to deliver an
intended result [ISO 9000]. | | Business | Role | A business role is the responsibility for performing specific behavior, to
which an actor can be assigned, or the part an actor plays in a
particular action or event. (Source: ArchiMate Specification) | | Business | Service-Level Agreements
(SLAs) | Essential components to operate data governance. They describe within
each business context the applicable level of service required to support
business use cases. For example, a data quality rule on an individual
email address may have different acceptable thresholds depending on
the business operating model: B2C or B2B2C. In the second scenario
(B2B2C), the quality of the email address may be irrelevant for the
company if they do not have any direct relationship with the customer. | | Operational | Data Access Event | Any event recorded in the information system to track access to a
subset of data by a user account. | | Operational | Data Quality Anomaly | An issue detected following the execution of a technical data quality
rule within the information system. | | Operational | Data Volume | Measure of the quantity of data within a data set or database. | | Operational | Metadata Activity Logs | A set of events related to any activity undertaken within the metadata
repository. | | Technical | Application | A classification of computer programs designed to perform specific
tasks, such as word processing, database management, or graphics. | | Technical | Data Flow | Describes the data flows between applications. | | Technical | Database | An organized collection of data, generally stored and accessed
electronically from a computer system. The Database Management
System (DBMS) is the software that interacts with end users,
applications, and the database itself to capture and analyze the data.
(Source: Wikipedia) |

| Category | Name | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | Technical | Data Field | A place where data can be stored. Commonly used to refer to a column
in a database or a field in a data entry form or web form. (Source:
Wikipedia) | | Technical | Data Set | A collection of related, discrete items of related data that may be
accessed individually or in combination or managed as a whole entity.
(Source: TechTarget) | | Technical | Technical Data Deletion Rule | The physical executable component (in most cases an SQL SELECT
statement) of the business data deletion rule description. It is the
responsibility of IT to design and develop data deletion rules that can
then be implemented, executed, and monitored within batch or near
real-time applications across the enterprise. Output of a data deletion
rule is the list of all business references (e.g., contract
references/numbers, employee references/numbers, vendor
references/numbers, etc.) that do not comply with the rule (e.g., the list
of all customers contact details that should not be kept in the BI &
Analytics platform). | | Technical | Technical Data Quality Rule | The physical executable component of the business data quality rule. It
is the responsibility of IT to design and develop data quality rules that
can then be implemented, executed, and monitored within batch or
near real-time applications across the enterprise. Output of a data
quality rule is the list of all business references (e.g., contract
references/numbers, employee references/numbers, vendor
references/numbers, etc.) that do not comply with the rule (e.g., the list
of all contract references for which the contract start date is not a valid
date). |
